strengths: Clear problem formulation with comprehensive related work analyzing limitations of existing VQ methods (Table 1)
Elegant and intuitive directional reparameterization approach (Eq. 8-9) that naturally converges to exact nearest-neighbor assignment
Thorough experimental validation across 5 datasets with multiple metrics (SSIM, PSNR, LPIPS, FID) in both compression and generation tasks
Practical advantages as drop-in replacement requiring no auxiliary losses or temperature schedules
Extensive ablation studies and supplementary material demonstrating reproducibility and robustness across batch sizes, learning rates, and variance values
Novel identification and analysis of codebook-latent misalignment as a key failure mode, with SF-DiVeQ providing automatic solution
Improved codebook replacement algorithm based on importance sampling that achieves faster and more stable utilization
weaknesses: Novelty is primarily incremental over NSVQ - core contribution reduces to changing noise direction from random v~N(0,I) to deterministic v_d = v + (c_i*-z), lacking fundamental innovation
Hyperparameter tuning claim is overstated: σ² must differ by task (10^-3 for VQ-VAE vs 10^-2 for VQGAN), contradicting the 'no hyperparameter tuning' positioning
Insufficient theoretical analysis: lacks formal justification for directional alignment beyond intuition, no convergence guarantees, and mechanism for SF-DiVeQ's misalignment avoidance is hand-wavy
Confounding experimental factors: improved codebook replacement algorithm applied to all baselines except SF-DiVeQ makes it unclear how much gain comes from DiVeQ itself vs. the new replacement
SF-DiVeQ undermines 'drop-in replacement' claim requiring: 2-epoch quantization skip, careful initialization (Eq. 14), codebook usage tracking, and different initialization strategy than baselines

Modest improvements in multiple scenarios: VQGAN FID improvements often small and paper acknowledges small batch size training 'is less likely to highlight robustness', with only 3 runs and no error bars

Missing investigation into failure modes: NSVQ's catastrophic VQGAN performance (~70 FID) unexplained, RT's low-bitrate failures unanalyzed, and hard VQ inference differences from training inadequately discussed
Gradient equation (Eq. 10) uses stop gradients ambiguously; unclear if this provides sufficient gradient signal compared to alternatives

strengths: Clear problem formulation with comprehensive related work comparison (Table 1)
Solid experimental evaluation with multiple datasets, tasks, and metrics (SSIM, PSNR, LPIPS, FID)
Extensive ablation studies on batch size, learning rate, variance, and variants
Insightful analysis of codebook-latent misalignment phenomenon
Practical utility as drop-in replacement without auxiliary losses or temperature schedules
Thorough implementation details and reproducibility support in appendices
weaknesses: Limited novelty: core contribution (directed noise) is incremental over NSVQ (Vali & Bäckström, 2022); the fundamental idea of adding noise to simulate quantization is unchanged
Contradictory 'no hyperparameter tuning' claim: σ² must be set differently for different tasks (10^-3 for compression vs 10^-2 for generation) and varies across settings
Unfair experimental comparisons: SF-DiVeQ omits codebook replacement while baselines use it; suspicious NSVQ failure on VQGAN (FID ≈81.5 vs ≈6) suggests suboptimal baseline tuning
Lack of theoretical rigor: no convergence analysis; claim of 'unbiased codebook gradients' (Table 1) lacks proof; implications of stop-gradient operators in Eq. 10 unexplored
Misalignment analysis is operationally defined without theoretical justification; why SF-DiVeQ avoids it is intuitive but not formally proven
Missing statistical significance testing: results averaged over 3 runs without error bars or confidence intervals; some improvements appear modest
Limited evaluation scope: all experiments on images only despite VQ use in audio/video/speech domains; σ² values may not transfer to other domains
SF-DiVeQ contribution is incremental, leveraging SFVQ from same authors; main novelty is directional application to space-filling VQ
SF-DiVeQ requires complex initialization (skip quantization for epochs, careful codebook setup) contradicting 'simple drop-in' narrative
Missing comparisons: recent structured quantization methods (FSQ, RPQ, BSQ, LFQ) mentioned but not experimentally evaluated

strengths: Clear problem formulation with comprehensive review of 6 baseline methods and detailed characterization of their limitations (Table 1)
Elegant directional reparameterization technique (Eq. 8) that maintains geometric consistency with nearest-neighbor operation while enabling gradient flow
Novel SF-DiVeQ extension addressing codebook collapse without replacement heuristics, with compelling evidence of superior codebook-latent alignment (Fig. 4)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 5 datasets, multiple metrics (SSIM, PSNR, LPIPS, FID), 6 baselines, extensive ablations (batch size, learning rate, variance), and Residual VQ generalization tests
Insightful analysis identifying codebook misalignment as previously unrecognized failure mode in existing methods, with theoretical connection to rate-distortion violations
Strong reproducibility: detailed implementation specifications, 3-run averaging, drop-in replacement design requiring minimal code changes
Consistent improvements across VQ-VAE compression task (5-10% LPIPS reduction) and multiple datasets (CELEBA-HQ, FFHQ, AFHQ, LSUN variants)
weaknesses: Limited novelty: core contribution is incremental modification of NSVQ (Eq. 7), replacing random noise with directional noise vd = v + (ci* - z), representing modest conceptual advance
Contradicts 'no hyperparameter tuning' claim: σ² requires task-specific setting (10⁻³ for VQ-VAE, 10⁻² for VQGAN), with Fig. 20-21 showing performance sensitivity to this choice

Lacks theoretical rigor: no formal error bounds for directional reparameterization, SF-DiVeQ's misalignment prevention relies on intuition rather than rigorous analysis, connection to rate-distortion theory feels post-hoc
VQGAN generation results inconsistent: Table 2 shows non-monotonic FID with increasing bitrate; NSVQ's catastrophic performance (81.5 FID at bitrate 8) raises baseline implementation concerns

SF-DiVeQ initialization overhead contradicts simplicity claims: requires skipping VQ for initial epochs, careful averaging of recent latents (20-50 iterations), and continuous codebook usage tracking (Appendix A.5)

Comparison fairness concerns: proposed codebook replacement differs from baselines (importance sampling vs. random), RT required extensive tuning across decay rates, unclear if implementation gaps exist across methods
Missing statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests despite averaging over 3 runs; some improvements appear within potential noise margins
Marginal quantitative gains in many scenarios: ~10-15% LPIPS improvement, minimal gains at higher bitrates, unclear practical benefit justifying added complexity

Presentation issues: critical insights scattered across 36-page paper with appendices, circular logic in misalignment analysis (Sec. 4, C.6), lack of design justifications (e.g., stop gradient placement)

Incomplete coverage: FSQ/RPQ/BSQ/LFQ omitted from comparisons, no computational cost analysis, missing guidance on when to use DiVeQ vs. SF-DiVeQ, limited discussion of post-2022 relevance as diffusion models gain dominance

strengths: Comprehensive empirical evaluation across three diverse tasks (compression, generation, speech coding) with five image datasets and multiple evaluation metrics per task, demonstrating consistent improvements
Excellent structured analysis of existing VQ methods (Table 1) clearly identifying limitations of STE, EMA, RT, ST-GS, and NSVQ approaches
Practical advantages: drop-in replacement for VQ layers without auxiliary losses, complex temperature schedules, or train-test mismatches
Thorough ablation studies including variance sensitivity (C.5), batch size effects (C.3), learning rate effects (C.4), and codebook replacement contribution (C.6)
Useful analysis and visualization of codebook-latent misalignment problem, showing SF-DiVeQ avoids this issue better than competitors
Strong reproducibility: comprehensive implementation details, promised code release, multi-run experiments
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: the reparameterization trick is well-established (Kingma & Welling 2013), and the contribution over NSVQ is primarily directional alignment of noise, which is intuitive but incremental

Mathematical rigor lacking: the convergence claim (Eq. 9) that z_q → c_i* as σ² → 0 is stated informally; the use of stop_gradient on the normalized direction (Eq. 8) is ad-hoc and lacks theoretical justification; no gradient flow analysis or convergence guarantees provided

Hyperparameter contradiction: despite claiming σ² requires no tuning, the paper uses different values for different applications (10⁻³ for compression/speech, 10⁻² for generation), which constitutes task-specific selection

Experimental confound from codebook replacement strategy: the improved codebook replacement is applied to all baselines but not SF-DiVeQ, making it unclear how much improvement comes from the VQ method vs. the replacement strategy; ablation only shown for one configuration
Statistical significance not established: no error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical tests despite three independent runs; some performance differences between methods appear marginal
Incomplete baseline comparisons: no empirical evaluation of FSQ (Mentzer et al. 2023) and LFQ (Yu et al. 2023); RT required multiple tuning attempts (Section A.5), raising fairness concerns

SF-DiVeQ is not truly a drop-in replacement: requires custom initialization (skip 2 epochs, then initialize from recent latent means) and higher codebook learning rate for random initialization, adding complexity

Theoretical understanding shallow: no convergence analysis, gradient property analysis, or explanation of why this specific noise formulation leads to better optimization; paper lacks theoretical justification for empirical success

strengths: Comprehensive empirical evaluation across three applications and five datasets with extensive ablations and reproducibility details
Clever geometric solution to NSVQ's directional fidelity problem via directional reparameterization (Equation 8)
Valuable analysis of codebook-latent misalignment problem using rate-distortion theory (Section C.8, Figure 4)
Thorough structured review of existing VQ methods with clear limitations table (Table 1)
Well-motivated SF-DiVeQ extension addressing codebook collapse without heuristic replacement strategies
weaknesses: Limited novelty: Core contribution is relatively straightforward modification of NSVQ (adding constant offset to noise), presented as incremental combination of prior work rather than fundamental advance

Theoretical gaps: Weak connection between stated reparameterization trick framework and actual method; unclear why directional offset is principled solution; missing rigorous analysis of gradient flow through non-differentiable arg min operation

Marginal empirical improvements: Figure 6 and Table 2 show small gaps vs. STE/EMA baselines; largest improvements are vs. NSVQ/RT (less mature methods); no statistical significance testing despite claims of consistent improvement

Contradicts simplicity claims: σ² requires task-dependent tuning (10⁻³ vs 10⁻²); SF-DiVeQ needs custom initialization, higher codebook learning rates, and tracking of usage percentage—undermining drop-in replacement narrative

Experimental design concerns: Codebook replacement strategy applied to all baselines conflates improvements; inconsistent initialization between SF-DiVeQ and other methods; limited baseline comparisons (FSQ/LFQ mentioned but not compared); no evaluation beyond standard applications

SF-DiVeQ robustness issues: Random initialization significantly underperforms (Figure 24); requires learning rate adjustments (Figure 25); high sensitivity to initialization contradicts claimed simplicity despite custom initialization (Equation 14)

Limited theoretical understanding: Missing principled explanation for why directional alignment helps; misalignment prevention argument relies on intuition rather than rigorous analysis; no convergence properties or gradient flow guarantees analyzed

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three diverse applications (VQ-VAE compression, VQGAN generation, DAC speech coding) with 5 image datasets and speech data, showing consistent improvements with multiple appropriate metrics

Elegant core contribution using the reparameterization trick to create a differentiable VQ approximation that preserves hard assignments while enabling gradient flow, with clear mathematical formulation and limit analysis (Eq. 9)

Exceptionally thorough ablation studies examining variance sensitivity, batch size robustness, learning rate effects, codebook replacement contribution, SF-DiVeQ initialization, and application to Residual VQ

Identifies and addresses multiple related problems: gradient collapse, codebook collapse, and codebook-latent misalignment, with SF-DiVeQ novel in preventing misalignment without replacement heuristics

Strong practical utility: no auxiliary losses, minimal hyperparameter tuning (σ² robust for σ² ≤ 10⁻²), drop-in replacement capability, and reproducibility via code release and detailed hyperparameters
Systematic review of existing VQ optimization methods (Table 1) with clear explanation of limitations and how the proposed method addresses them
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and well-organized narrative flow
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: applying the reparameterization trick from VAEs to VQ is conceptually straightforward, and SF-DiVeQ substantially builds on prior work (Vali & Backström 2023a)

Hyperparameter requirement overstated: despite claims of 'no complicated parameter tuning,' σ² must be set differently for different tasks (10⁻³ for compression, 10⁻² for generation), contradicting the no-tuning claim

SF-DiVeQ complexity contradicts 'drop-in replacement' claim: requires 2-epoch warm-up, careful initialization from recent latents with specific guidelines (Eq. 14), and higher codebook learning rates for random init (Fig. 25)

Comparison fairness concerns: new codebook replacement strategy (B.1) applied to all baselines except SF-DiVeQ; this could give unfair advantage and may explain surprisingly poor NSVQ performance (Table 2: FID > 40)
Insufficient investigation of NSVQ baseline weakness: NSVQ performance is suspiciously poor given it is the most similar method; implementation or hyperparameter differences not explored

Limited theoretical analysis: no justification for this specific reparameterization over alternatives, no approximation error bounds, no convergence analysis, and stop gradient design choices not explained
Evaluation limitations: VQGAN uses FID only (missing IS, precision/recall), speech subjective samples not in main paper, computational overhead and training time not reported
Misalignment analysis relies primarily on t-SNE visualization; quantitative dispersion metrics and deeper root-cause analysis would strengthen claims
No statistical rigor: missing error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests despite claims about improvements often in 2-5% range
